# Third-Party Notices

Parts of Experience Skills adapt ideas and data from the open-source projects below. The adapted
material was rewritten and reorganized; no files were copied verbatim. Both projects are released
under the MIT License, whose notice is reproduced here as that license requires for substantial
portions. Experience Skills itself is also MIT-licensed.

## Hallmark

- Repository: https://github.com/Nutlope/hallmark
- Commit reviewed: 13ac0ec7e148655948100b6396439e481361d690 (2026-09-24)
- License: MIT (root LICENSE; no nested licenses found)
- What was adapted, in rewritten form:
  - The idea of choosing a named page shape ("macrostructure") from an index and loading only that
    description; several page-shape concepts (long document, stat-led, workbench, split narrative,
    sticky feature stack, map/diagram, index-first, catalog, ecosystem index, component playground)
    rewritten as compositions with content requirements, states, responsive and RTL behavior, and
    failure conditions (`compositions-index.md`, `compositions-narrative.md`, and related files).
  - The practice of varying structure between outputs and offering choices from different categories
    (`selection.md`).
  - The "study" idea of extracting a reference's design DNA instead of copying it (`selection.md`).
  - The practice of a self-critique pass before presenting work (reflected in skill checkpoints).
- Not used: themes, components, screenshots, site examples, copy, and code.

## UI UX Pro Max

- Repository: https://github.com/nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max-skill
- Commit reviewed: dcc40ff5133ef78276117db0cc34e7b83cc8aeba (2026-09-24)
- License: MIT (root LICENSE). A nested Apache-2.0 license applies to the repository's
  `.claude/skills/ui-styling` and `cli/assets/skills/ui-styling` folders; nothing from those folders
  was used.
- What was adapted, in rewritten form:
  - Chart-selection guidance by data type, including "when not to use" conditions
    (`data-visualization.md`).
  - A curated subset of font pairings (font names and pairing choices), reorganized by character
    instead of industry (`typography.md`).
  - The style catalog was reviewed as a coverage check for the design-direction library; directions
    were written independently, and several catalog styles were reclassified as surface treatments
    (`surfaces-and-shape.md`).
- Not used: color palettes by product type, product-to-style mappings, UX guideline rows, code,
  templates, scripts, and screenshots.
